processing: A top grade made only from the upper leaves of the bush and containing tips, finished as black tea. The same name also marks the top of the Georgian green tea scale.
harvest_season: Made from the uppermost young leaves; a specific season is not recorded.
appearance_dry: Clean dark leaf with visible tips.
appearance_liquor: Clear amber, lighter than Indian or Ceylon black, as is general for Georgian tea.
appearance_wet: Small, even, coppery young leaves, as expected from upper-leaf picking.
taste_profile: Aromatic and soft rather than sharp, as with good Georgian black tea in general.

brewing.notes: Georgian tea extracts quickly and colours lightly. For a stronger cup use more leaf, 1.5 to 2 teaspoons per cup, not more time. Blending it with Indian or Ceylon tea hides its own taste.

vintage_note: It was a named grade rather than a vintage product, and no sale by harvest year is documented. If a modern tin carries the name, ask for the harvest year and producer, and treat it like other black tea, best within a couple of years.
description:
Georgian Bouquet, Buket Gruzii in Russian, was the top name in the old Georgian tea grading, the level above the ordinary sorts. It marks a quality grade, not a place or a particular bush.

For black tea, Bouquet and Extra sat at the very top for quality and cleanness. They were made only from the upper leaves of the bush and contained tips, which is what separated them from the cut-leaf higher grade below.

Georgian black tea descends mainly from Chinese Keemun-type material, and in the cup it is typically fragrant and gentle with a lighter colour than Indian or Ceylon. It extracts fast, so add leaf rather than time for strength.

The name also appears in Georgian green tea, above the numbered scale that ran up to No. 125, so check which colour you are holding if you find an old pack.
history: Georgian Bouquet is documented as part of the older Georgian grade system, at the top of both the black and the green ranges. Little is recorded about who introduced the name, or when.
